tokens.name: --default-transition-duration
tokens.section: Motion. Until this landed, theme.css bridged colour, radius and type but nothing about movement, so every `transition-*` utility in the app silently ran Tailwind's stock ease-out at 150ms while the rest of the product ran --ae-ease at 130ms. Overriding the two defaults means a bare `transition-colors` is on the brand curve without anyone opting in, and `ease-quiet` names the curve for the cases that set it explicitly. There is deliberately no `duration-*` alias: Tailwind v4 has no such theme namespace, and the supported spelling is the custom-property shorthand, `duration-(--ae-dur)` / `duration-(--ae-dur-fast)`.

tokens.name: --paper-affordance
tokens.section: Simulated paper The one light surface the product owns. Résumé previews, the live document editor and the schema atlas all draw a printed page inside a dark-only app, and the --ae-* ramp cannot express that: --ae-fg on white is invisible and --ae-border on white is not there. These are the page's own ink, not a second theme, and nothing outside a document preview may use them. --paper-affordance carries the editor's own controls sitting on the page (drag grips, empty hints, field stubs). Those are app chrome that happens to land on the document, so they answer to the app's contrast standard: 6.0:1 on white. Its predecessor was 3.21:1 and axe caught it.

tokens.section: Type scale. Without these, `text-sm` silently resolves to Tailwind's own 0.875rem instead of Quiet's 12px, and the only way to hit a token size from a utility is a hardcoded px value, which the identity forbids.
